findings.title: Translated paragraphs list grows by append although its length is known, breaking the AGENTS.md sizing rule
findings.failureScenario: Any `postilla translate` run on a story with N Italian paragraphs fills `done` with exactly N+1 entries: the title paragraph, then one per paragraph. `done` starts as `.empty` and grows through `try done.append(a, ...)` once per paragraph. Each paragraph's request body, user message, reply and parsed array are allocated in the same arena between appends, so every time the list grows, the arena cannot resize it in place. It copies the list into a new buffer and leaves the old one allocated until the run ends. The impact is a few wasted kilobytes plus extra copies per language, not a crash. It breaks a written AGENTS.md rule, which mr-review counts as a finding.
findings.evidence: src/cli.zig:227 `var done: std.ArrayList([]const []const u8) = .empty;` and src/cli.zig:238 `try done.append(a, for (0..3) |_| { ... })` inside `for (0..it.paragraphs.len + 1) |p|`. AGENTS.md:9: "when the length is known, size an `ArrayList` once (`ensureTotalCapacity`) or allocate the slice once." AGENTS.md:27: "Fail early: acquire buffers and resources up front".
findings.fix: Allocate the slice once: `const done = try a.alloc([]const []const u8, it.paragraphs.len + 1);`. Assign each paragraph with `done[p] = for (0..3) |_| { ... } else return fail(...);` and use `done[0][0]`, `done[0][1]` and `done[1..]` at line 249.
findings.reason:
I could not refute it. The report reads the code correctly. In src/cli.zig, `done` starts as `.empty` (line 227) and grows by `try done.append(a, ...)` once per iteration of `for (0..it.paragraphs.len + 1)`. So its final length, paragraphs.len + 1, is known before the loop starts. Each iteration allocates the request body, the user message, the reply and the parsed array in arena `a`, so each growth of the list copies it and leaves the old buffer allocated until the arena is freed.

The base diff shows these lines were added by this feature. Nothing upstream sizes the list, and no test checks for this.

AGENTS.md line 9 says that when the length is known, an ArrayList is sized once with ensureTotalCapacity or the slice is allocated once. RULES.md says the stage 2 hunt uses the AGENTS.md checklist, so a rule breach is in scope. One point in its favour does not refute it: AGENTS.md calls the CLI a cold path to keep simple. That line does not exempt it from the sizing rule.

Rating:
- Chance: common. It happens on every translate run, for every language.
- Criticality: minor. It is not a bug. The output is correct, and the only cost is a few kilobytes and some copies, freed when the run's arena is freed.
- Silent: no. There is no wrong result to go unnoticed, so the rule that a silent minor counts as major does not apply.
- Fix: about 1 added line, `try done.ensureTotalCapacity(a, it.paragraphs.len + 1);` before the loop, with `append` changed to `appendAssumeCapacity`. Another option is to allocate the slice once and assign `done[p]`.
findings.reproReason: The finding is about how memory is allocated, and nothing a user can see changes because of it. `cli.run` (src/cli.zig:30) takes one arena from `main` and frees it when the process exits. Growing `done` by `append` (src/cli.zig:227-245) only means a few extra copies and a few KB held until exit. The 20 000-character cap on the Italian text keeps `done` to a few hundred 16-byte slices. Whether `done` is sized up front or grown by append, the exit code, stdout, the request bytes sent to OpenCode and the bytes of story.json are all the same, and no leak is possible because the arena owns everything. The only ways to show it would be to count allocations or bytes held in the arena (internal state, which TESTING.md bans asserting on) or to run under a deliberately tiny fixed-buffer allocator (a state the real binary never runs in). The issue is a real break of the AGENTS.md:9 rule that a list whose length is known gets sized once, but that makes it a review or rule finding, not a bug a test can reproduce. No repro file was written, so there was nothing to delete, and no production code was changed.
